description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of various entity types identified in a biomedical named entity recognition task, with each slice representing a distinct category and its corresponding proportion of the total. The largest segment, colored blue, corresponds to "Chemical" entities, accounting for 32% of the total. The second largest segment, orange, represents "Protein" entities at 15%. "DNA" entities are shown in green and make up 6% of the distribution. "Chemical Family" and "Disease" entities, both in red and purple respectively, each constitute 5% of the total. "Cell Type" entities, in brown, account for 5%, while "Drug" entities, in pink, represent 4%. Several categories are each represented by 3% of the total: "Frequency" (gray), "Cell Line" (yellow), and "Dosage" (light blue). Smaller segments include "Strength" (dark blue) at 2%, "Gene Or Gene Product" (green) at 2%, "Form" (light green) at 2%, and "Disease Or Phenotypic Feature" (light purple) at 2%. The remaining categories— "Route" (brown), "Reason" (gray), "Sequence Variant" (pink), "Modifier" (light pink), "RNA" (light blue), "Disease Class" (light green), "Organism Taxon" (light green), "Duration" (light green), and "Composite Mention" (light green)—are each represented by 1% of the total. The chart uses distinct colors for each category, with labels and percentage values clearly displayed next to or inside the corresponding slices, and a legend is not required as the labels are directly attached to the slices.
